// Shared per-spec data setup. Each spec's beforeEach RESETS then SEEDS via the app's /__test__
// endpoint — this is Arrange, not Assert. Specs still ASSERT only through the UI (data-testid).
//
// FAIL LOUD: /__test__/reset and /__test__/seed are the Arrange for EVERY spec, so they are a hard
// precondition — if either does not return 2xx the data is not in the state the test assumes, and a
// silent failure would surface later as confusing, misattributed assertion failures on unrelated
// specs (e.g. leftover rows because reset could not clear an FK-referenced table). We throw here so
// the break is attributed to the seed contract, and so a developer running its own spec sees the
// broken endpoint immediately instead of shipping it.
import { request, type APIResponse } from '@playwright/test';

const BASE = process.env.BASE_URL ?? `http://localhost:${process.env.PORT ?? 3000}`;

async function must(res: Promise<APIResponse>, what: string): Promise<void> {
  const r = await res;
  if (!r.ok()) {
    const body = (await r.text().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 500);
    throw new Error(`seed contract broken: ${what} returned HTTP ${r.status()} — ${body}`);
  }
}

export async function resetAndSeed(fixture: unknown): Promise<void> {
  const api = await request.newContext({ baseURL: BASE });
  try {
    await must(api.post('/__test__/reset'), 'POST /__test__/reset');
    await must(api.post('/__test__/seed', { data: fixture }), 'POST /__test__/seed');
  } finally {
    await api.dispose();
  }
}

// Usage in a spec:
//   test.beforeEach(async () => { await resetAndSeed({ /* rows this spec needs */ }); });

import { Route, Router, RouterLink, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router';
import { GlobalSearch } from './features/search/global-search';

// Minimal base shell. It renders the nav bar and the routed page. The nav comes from the ROUTER'S
// OWN CONFIG — every route carrying `data.section` becomes a link — so the shell holds no list of
// pages and is not edited when one is added. Every observable element carries a stable data-testid.
@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [RouterOutlet, RouterLink, GlobalSearch],
  template: `
    <div data-testid="app-root">
      <nav data-testid="app-nav">
        @for (r of nav; track r.path) {
          <a
            [routerLink]="'/' + r.path"
            [attr.data-testid]="'nav-' + r.data!['section']"
            >{{ r.data!['label'] }}</a
          >
        }
      </nav>
      <app-global-search />
      <main data-testid="app-home">
        <router-outlet />
      </main>
    </div>
  `,
})
export class App {
  protected readonly nav: Route[] = inject(Router)
    .config.filter((r) => !!r.data?.['section'])
    .sort(
      (a, b) =>
        ((a.data?.['order'] as number) ?? 0) - ((b.data?.['order'] as number) ?? 0) ||
        String(a.data?.['section']).localeCompare(String(b.data?.['section'])),
    );
}

// Shared per-spec data setup. Each spec's beforeEach RESETS then SEEDS via the app's /__test__
// endpoint — this is Arrange, not Assert. Specs still ASSERT only through the UI (data-testid).
//
// FAIL LOUD: /__test__/reset and /__test__/seed are the Arrange for EVERY spec, so they are a hard
// precondition — if either does not return 2xx the data is not in the state the test assumes, and a
// silent failure would surface later as confusing, misattributed assertion failures on unrelated
// specs (e.g. leftover rows because reset could not clear an FK-referenced table). We throw here so
// the break is attributed to the seed contract, and so a developer running its own spec sees the
// broken endpoint immediately instead of shipping it.
import { request, type APIResponse } from '@playwright/test';

const BASE = process.env.BASE_URL ?? `http://localhost:${process.env.PORT ?? 3000}`;

async function must(res: Promise<APIResponse>, what: string): Promise<void> {
  const r = await res;
  if (!r.ok()) {
    const body = (await r.text().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 500);
    throw new Error(`seed contract broken: ${what} returned HTTP ${r.status()} — ${body}`);
  }
}

export async function resetAndSeed(fixture: unknown): Promise<void> {
  const api = await request.newContext({ baseURL: BASE });
  try {
    await must(api.post('/__test__/reset'), 'POST /__test__/reset');
    await must(api.post('/__test__/seed', { data: fixture }), 'POST /__test__/seed');
  } finally {
    await api.dispose();
  }
}

import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

// The route table. A page is a new component file registered here with one entry that lazily
// imports it; an entry's `data: { section, label }` is read by the shell to build the nav bar.
export const routes: Routes = [
  { path: '', redirectTo: 'home', pathMatch: 'full' },
  {
    path: 'home',
    data: { section: 'home', label: 'Home', order: 0 },
    loadComponent: () => import('./features/home/home').then((m) => m.Home),
  },
  {
    path: 'dashboard',
    data: { section: 'dashboard', label: 'Dashboard', order: 0 },
    loadComponent: () => import('./features/dashboard/dashboard').then((m) => m.Dashboard),
  },
  {
    path: 'clients',

    loadComponent: () => import('./features/clients/clients').then((m) => m.Clients),
  },
  {
    path: 'clients/:id',
    // Wait for a payment being recorded to be saved before leaving, so other pages see it.
    canDeactivate: [(page: { canLeave(): Promise<boolean> }) => page.canLeave()],

import { Component, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { Route, Router, RouterLink, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router';
import { GlobalSearch } from './features/search/global-search';

// Minimal base shell. It renders the nav bar and the routed page. The nav comes from the ROUTER'S
// OWN CONFIG — every route carrying `data.section` becomes a link — so the shell holds no list of
// pages and is not edited when one is added. Every observable element carries a stable data-testid.
@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [RouterOutlet, RouterLink, GlobalSearch],
  template: `
    <div data-testid="app-root">
      <nav data-testid="app-nav">
        @for (r of nav; track r.path) {
          <a
            [routerLink]="'/' + r.path"
            [attr.data-testid]="'nav-' + r.data!['section']"
            >{{ r.data!['label'] }}</a
          >
        }
      </nav>
      <app-global-search />
      <main data-testid="app-home">
        <router-outlet />
      </main>
    </div>
  `,
})
export class App {
  protected readonly nav: Route[] = inject(Router)
    .config.filter((r) => !!r.data?.['section'])
    .sort(
      (a, b) =>
        ((a.data?.['order'] as number) ?? 0) - ((b.data?.['order'] as number) ?? 0) ||
        String(a.data?.['section']).localeCompare(String(b.data?.['section'])),

**How they're worked out** (both count from 1 January to today):
- **Billed this year** adds up sent invoices issued this year, the same way the existing "Billed this month" figure does. Drafts and cancelled invoices are left out.
- **Collected this year** adds up every payment dated this year. A payment in another currency is converted at the rate on its invoice's issue date, matching how the existing collection-rate figure converts. A payment that can't be converted is left out.

**What changed:**
- **Server:** `DashboardService` works out the two figures and returns them as `billingsYearToDate` and `collectedYearToDate` from `/api/dashboard`. `PaymentRepository` got a new query, `findByDateBetween`, to fetch the payments in a date range.

- **Database:** no migration was needed, because both figures come from data the app already stores.

**Decision for you:** "Collected this year" counts a payment by the date it was received, even if its invoice was issued last year. So the two figures don't pair up invoice by invoice. If you'd rather count only payments on invoices issued this year, it's a small change.
